name: Cerebras WSE-3 / WSE-3 Turbo (CS-3, CS-4)
memory_bandwidth_basis: CS-3 system page states 44 GB on-chip SRAM and 21 PB/s memory bandwidth for the wafer, i.e. ~21,000 GB/s of on-wafer SRAM bandwidth. IMPORTANT: vram_gb here holds the ON-CHIP SRAM CAPACITY, not VRAM or HBM. The WSE-3 Turbo in CS-4 is quoted at 43.2 PB/s, roughly 2x.
notes: WAFFER-SCALE, so per-chip reasoning does not apply and neither does the GPU mental model. A WSE is one 215 mm square reticle-sized piece of silicon, the largest AI semiconductor ever built, built by TSMC; it is a single device, not a cluster of cards. WHAT IS IN vram_gb: 44 GB of on-chip SRAM (CS-3 page) rather than any HBM or GDDR. THE MEMORY HIERARCHY IS THE WHOLE POINT: SRAM-only with no DRAM tier means weight streaming from off-package is impossible and the roofline shifts entirely. Decode arithmetic intensity at batch 1 is set by 21-43 PB/s of on-wafer bandwidth against ~125-250 PFLOPS of compute, a ratio near 3-6 FLOP/byte, so at batch 1 this is a bandwidth-bound machine with an enormous bandwidth and a very small capacity. That combination only makes sense because the whole working set is resident on the wafer: for a 70B model in FP16 the weights are ~140 GB, which is why Cerebras sells multi-wafer systems and why the per-wafer figure is meaningless in isolation. Scale-out is by adding wafers: CS-4 puts three WSE-3 Turbo wafers in one system, reducing wafer-to-wafer interconnect latency to 2 microseconds, which is the mechanism that keeps decode interactive as models exceed 10T parameters. flops is recorded at 125 PFLOPS (half of the 250 PFLOPS headline) with dense:false, because the CS-4 page states '250 PFLOPS of compute' without a precision label and the FP16 halving is an assumption, not a vendor statement. It should be read as 'system-level throughput in an unstated precision, halved, and marked non-comparable'. Other figures: 900,000 AI-optimised cores, 4 trillion transistors, 214 Pb/s on-wafer interconnect, 1.2 Tb/s system I/O, 16RU, ~25 kW per node and up to ~USD 3M per node. Cost and power are the reason this sits in a niche. NOTE ON GENERATION: WSE-3 launched in 2022 in CS-3; CS-4 (Aug 2026) uses the faster WSE-3 Turbo variant at up to 2x the prior generation's speed per wafer. Marketing claim of 'up to 30x faster inference than GPU systems' is vendor-internal benchmarking plus Artificial Analysis and is not a hardware specification.
